description: Unofficial: Australian economic data from the ABS, RBA and APRA. CPI, GDP, cash rate, jobs and more.

tools.name: list_catalogue
tools.description:
List curated ABS, RBA, and APRA catalogue entries, optionally filtered by source,
category, or tag. Unranked complement to search_datasets.

include_discontinued.description: Whether to include discontinued RBA catalogue entries.

tools.name: get_abs_data
tools.description:
Expert/source-native ABS SDMX retrieval in a normalised response shape.

Curated indicators from ABS dataflows, such as CPI inflation, the unemployment rate and
GDP growth, are also available through get_economic_series, which can return several in
one result and one chart.

In MCP Apps hosts (claude.ai, Claude Desktop) a result with up to eight series is
already shown to the user as an interactive chart with a data table, so another chart
of the same data would duplicate it.

key.description: ABS SDMX key, or "all" for all series.

start_period.description: Optional ABS period bound in YYYY, YYYY-QN, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-SN format.

end_period.description: Optional ABS period bound in YYYY, YYYY-QN, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-SN format.

last_n.description: Optional limit returning only the most recent N observations per series; metadata.truncated is true when older observations were dropped.

updated_after.description: Optional ISO date or datetime accepted by the ABS updatedAfter API.

include_observation_dimensions.description: Whether to repeat the full dimension dict on every observation. Off by default because the same dimensions already appear on each series descriptor and are encoded in series_id.

tools.name: list_rba_tables
tools.description:
Deprecated compatibility alias. list_catalogue(source="rba") returns the same
curated RBA tables.

include_discontinued.description: Whether to include discontinued RBA catalogue entries.

tools.name: get_rba_table
tools.description:
Expert/source-native RBA statistical table retrieval in a normalised response shape.

Curated indicators from RBA tables, such as the cash rate target, mortgage rates, bond
yields and credit growth, are also available through get_economic_series, which can
return several in one result and one chart.

In MCP Apps hosts (claude.ai, Claude Desktop) a result with up to eight series is
already shown to the user as an interactive chart with a data table, so another chart
of the same data would duplicate it.

series_ids.description: Optional list of non-empty source-native series IDs to keep after download.

start_date.description: Optional ISO date bound in YYYY-MM-DD format.

end_date.description: Optional ISO date bound in YYYY-MM-DD format.

last_n.description: Optional limit returning only the most recent N observations per series; metadata.truncated is true when older observations were dropped.

include_observation_dimensions.description: Whether to repeat the full dimension dict on every observation. Off by default because the same dimensions already appear on each series descriptor and are encoded in series_id.

tools.name: get_apra_data
tools.description:
Expert/source-native APRA public XLSX publication retrieval.

Only curated official APRA publication IDs are accepted; arbitrary URLs are not.

Curated indicators from APRA publications, such as bank capital ratios and housing loan
exposures, are also available through get_economic_series, which can return several in
one result and one chart.

In MCP Apps hosts (claude.ai, Claude Desktop) a result with up to eight series is
already shown to the user as an interactive chart with a data table, so another chart
of the same data would duplicate it.

anyOf.description: Table within an APRA publication, such as table_1 (APRA only).

table_id.description: Table within an APRA publication, such as table_1 (APRA only).

series_ids.description: Optional list of non-empty source-native series IDs to keep after download.

start_date.description: Optional ISO date bound in YYYY-MM-DD format.

end_date.description: Optional ISO date bound in YYYY-MM-DD format.

last_n.description: Optional limit returning only the most recent N observations per series; metadata.truncated is true when older observations were dropped.

include_observation_dimensions.description: Whether to repeat the full dimension dict on every observation. Off by default because the same dimensions already appear on each series descriptor and are encoded in series_id.

tools.name: get_economic_series
tools.description:
Main analyst-facing retrieval tool for curated ABS, RBA and APRA concepts.

list_economic_concepts lists the accepted concepts. Date bounds accept YYYY, YYYY-QN,
YYYY-SN, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD and are normalised to the resolved source.

A list of up to eight concepts returns them together in one result, which MCP Apps
hosts display as one chart.

In MCP Apps hosts (claude.ai, Claude Desktop) a result with up to eight series is
already shown to the user as an interactive chart with a data table, so another chart
of the same data would duplicate it.

concept.description: Curated semantic concept name, or a list of up to eight to retrieve together.

variant.description: Optional curated concept variant, such as headline, underlying, or target.

geography.description: Optional geography selector for a curated concept, usually aus for Australia.

frequency.description: Optional published frequency for a curated concept: daily, monthly, quarterly, annual or event-driven (or the codes D, M, Q, A, E). It selects among the frequencies a concept is published at and does not resample. With several concepts it applies to each concept published at that frequency; the others keep their default, noted in metadata.warnings.

start.description: Optional analyst-friendly date bound: YYYY, YYYY-QN, YYYY-SN, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD. Semantic retrieval normalises this to the resolved source frequency.

end.description: Optional analyst-friendly date bound: YYYY, YYYY-QN, YYYY-SN, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD. Semantic retrieval normalises this to the resolved source frequency.

last_n.description: Optional limit returning only the most recent N observations per series; metadata.truncated is true when older observations were dropped.

include_observation_dimensions.description: Whether to repeat the full dimension dict on every observation. Off by default because the same dimensions already appear on each series descriptor and are encoded in series_id.

tools.name: get_derived_series
tools.description:
Read-only retrieval for the narrow transparent derived series layer.

Date bounds accept YYYY, YYYY-QN, YYYY-SN, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD and
are normalised to the derived series frequency.

In MCP Apps hosts (claude.ai, Claude Desktop) a result with up to eight series is
already shown to the user as an interactive chart with a data table, so another chart
of the same data would duplicate it.

start.description: Optional analyst-friendly bound for a derived series: YYYY, YYYY-QN, YYYY-SN, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD. Bounds are normalised to the derived series frequency.

end.description: Optional analyst-friendly bound for a derived series: YYYY, YYYY-QN, YYYY-SN, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD. Bounds are normalised to the derived series frequency.

last_n.description: Optional limit returning only the most recent N observations per series; metadata.truncated is true when older observations were dropped.

tools.name: get_latest_observations
tools.description:
Source-aware convenience wrapper for the latest observations.

Without series_ids, a broad dataset returns every series it contains; series_ids
narrows it. get_economic_series(concept=...) returns a single curated indicator
as one series.

source.description: Source selector: abs (Australian Bureau of Statistics), rba (Reserve Bank of Australia) or apra (Australian Prudential Regulation Authority).

key.description: ABS SDMX key, or "all" for all series.

anyOf.description: Table within an APRA publication, such as table_1 (APRA only).

table_id.description: Table within an APRA publication, such as table_1 (APRA only).

series_ids.description: Optional list of non-empty source-native series IDs to keep after download.

count.description: Number of most recent observations to return per series; metadata.truncated is true when older observations were dropped.
